reading.body:
J-Curve Technologies is not a confirmed data center, so it cannot be counted toward Arizona's data center capacity or its grid load.

The entry rests on a single OpenStreetMap node tagged as a data center at coordinates in Tempe, Arizona. Reverse geocoding those coordinates returns only a building address on West 14th Street with no business name attached. No operator website, business registration, or press coverage naming J-Curve Technologies at that location could be confirmed, and the research status is recorded as exhausted. The name itself is more common in finance and economics than in the technology industry.

This matters for AI because facility counts are the denominator in any claim about compute growth and the power it draws. Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, and only 4 of them publish power specifications, totaling 512 MW. A row like this one sits in the unmapped remainder: it carries a location and a tag but no megawatts, no operator, and no evidence of servers. Adding it to a facility tally would overstate the physical footprint behind AI workloads, and adding it to a power tally is impossible because no capacity is published.

What the data does not say is whether any equipment exists at the address. It records an absence of confirmation, not a confirmed absence. The 56-facility and 512 MW figures describe what is mapped and published in Arizona, not what is built, and the gap between those two things is where this entry lives.
